label: Card Formats
description: Cards as printed artifacts — the frame, the furniture and the conventions each kind carries. What separates a tarot card from a trading card is not the picture but everything drawn around it.

items.name: tarot-major-arcana
items.text: a tarot major-arcana card: portrait frame with an ornamented border, a roman numeral at the top and a title banner at the foot, symbolic figure centred and staring out
items.text_short: tarot major arcana, ornate border, numeral

items.name: tcg-creature
items.text: a trading-card-game creature card: illustration window in the upper two thirds, name bar above it, a type line and a stat corner below, ornate rarity-coded frame
items.text_short: TCG creature card, illustration window, stat corner

items.name: sports-card
items.text: a sports trading card: action photograph bleeding to the edges, name plate across the bottom, small team crest, glossy chromed finish
items.text_short: sports card, bleed photo, name plate

items.name: playing-card-face
items.text: a playing-card court face: mirrored top-and-bottom composition, index pip in two opposite corners, flat heraldic colour
items.text_short: playing card court face, mirrored, corner pips

items.name: oracle-deck
items.text: an oracle card: soft full-bleed illustration with a single keyword set in generous type at the foot, thin metallic rule inside the trim
items.text_short: oracle card, full bleed, keyword foot

items.name: holo-foil-parallel
items.text: a holographic foil parallel: rainbow foil catching across the illustration in a directional sweep, the frame's flat areas left to shimmer

items.name: kickstarter-promo
items.text: a promo card: dramatic edge-to-edge art, a small numbered stamp in one corner, minimal frame furniture
